newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank seen holding rates at least to August.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank seen holding rates at least to August.

text.p: The Bank of Finland may hike its tender rate in the autumn to fend off inflation risks in Finland's fast-growing economy, but it would not act as long as markets are in summer doldrums, analysts said on Monday.

That would mean steady rates at least through July and maybe August, although some fear an early move next month, and say the September forward rate, at 3.29 percent, factors in most of a 0.25 point hike in the tender rate from 3.00 percent.
In mid-June, the central bank said that although the outlook did not yet call for a change in monetary policy, an increase in inflation risks could eventually force tightening.
"Doing it in the middle of the main holiday month (July) would indicate there was something really dramatic happening in our economy," Merita Bank analyst Mikko Ayub said on Monday.

Analysts said that if the Bank of Finland started raising rates -- which they also said would be more likely if the German Bundesbank were to hike its repo rate -- it would likely start with a 25 basis point increase, with more possibly to follow.

Protos Stockbrokers economist Petteri Hirvonen agreed that a hike now would focus special attention on the economy which is growing fast. The latest monthly GDP indicator showed year-on-year growth at 8.0 percent in April, and GDP growth forecasts range between four and five percent for this year.
"Obviously there is a risk of a rate hike, but not before August," Hirvonen said.
Economic data this week will give new hints of what the bank will do, analysts said.

For the bank to hike rates next month, June CPI inflation data due on Tuesday at 0700/0400 GMT would need to rise at least 0.3 percent month-on-month, versus a 0.1 percent average forecast, Hirvonen said.
He said industry output growth, also due early on Tuesday, would also have to be above forecasts which currently show a 7.4 percent year-on-year increase.

The central bank's inflation risk comments last month boosted forward rates, and September forward rate agreements (FRAs) now trade at 3.28 percent. The three-month spot money rate trades slightly below 3.10 percent.
The tender rate for one-month paper has been steady at 3.00 percent -- on a par with the German repo rate -- since October.
"A hike is now a matter of when rather than if," said Enskilda economist Mika Erkkila. "Our forecast is that it will come in the third quarter ... that would be in August."
He expected a 25 basis point move, but added that this would only be the first in the cycle.
"After a 25 basis points increase, another 25 basis points would be immediately discounted in FRA rates," said Hirvonen.

But the Bank of Finland also aims to maintain a stable currency, and with a weakening German mark, the key DEM/FIM rate has been moving further away from its 3.04 parity rate in the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM). Some analysts said the central bank may look for at least a correction before possibly acting.
"We think DEM/FIM will fall to some 2.90-2.95 after a rate hike but then rise again to 2.97 by the end of the year...as the German economy will begin to grow faster," said Erkkila.
On Monday, DEM/FIM fell to a 2.9570 five-month low from 2.9685 on Friday as the mark eased against its crosses and the dollar. -- Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 248, news@reuters.fi
